articles.title: AWS and Google Cloud add spending limits as coding agents drive usage
articles.summary: Cloud providers Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud have introduced spending limits to help developers manage usage costs driven by autonomous coding agents. AWS announced a monthly spend limit feature that pauses projects upon reaching the threshold, while Google Cloud launched Spend Caps for specific services. However, developers still lack a universal hard cut-off default that returns errors to prevent runaway bills.

articles.title: Nvidia-backed Reflection prepares powerful open AI model
articles.summary: Nvidia-backed Reflection is preparing an open-weight model designed to compete with leading Chinese systems while giving enterprises a cheaper alternative to closed models. The startup ultimately wants companies to build customized “AI factories” using their own data, Reflection models, and private compute.

articles.title: Anthropic commits $100M to train 10,000 AI engineers
articles.summary: Claude Frontier Academy is a $100 million program designed to train 10,000 engineers in deploying Claude inside enterprises. The program focuses on producing engineers with skills similar to Anthropic's own forward-deployed teams.

articles.title: I Tested 11 HTTP Resilience Libraries
articles.summary: An engineer tested eleven HTTP resilience libraries against a suite of twenty-one conformance scenarios covering retries, timeouts, circuit breaking, bulkheads, hedging, and request deduplication. The results showed that while basic single-policy features like standard retries pass universally, combining policies or handling concurrent events like caller cancellations during backoffs exposes widespread correctness failures across most implementations.

articles.title: Apple's New macOS Controls Are the First OS-Level Move Specifically Targeting AI Agent Risks
articles.summary: Apple has announced plans to tighten controls around macOS Full Disk Access, specifically citing the risks autonomous AI agents pose to user data. The company will introduce additional controls requiring explicit user action for apps requesting this level of access, marking the first time a major operating system vendor has updated its core access permissions because of agents. The move follows recent security incidents and disclosures involving Meta's Muse AI and the ChatGPT Mac app.

articles.title: Okta XAA Ecosystem Scales to 25+ Partners as AI Gateways Become the Identity Enforcement Layer
articles.summary: TrueFoundry integrated Okta's Cross App Access (XAA) protocol into its AI gateway, making the gateway an identity checkpoint that replaces static API keys with short-lived, task-scoped tokens. The Okta XAA ecosystem has grown to over 25 early adopters as the infrastructure layer increasingly adopts identity enforcement for AI agents. The protocol is built on the ID-JAG standard and functions as an open OAuth extension that acts as a vendor-neutral enforcement point.

articles.title: IBM brings agents from Google and Microsoft under one control plane
articles.summary: IBM's watsonx Orchestrate can now discover and manage agents built on Microsoft Foundry and Google Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform alongside Amazon Bedrock agents. A new Agent Identity feature also gives each agent its own verifiable enterprise identity.

articles.title: MCP stateless spec changes: what the 2026-07-28 revision means for servers
articles.summary: The 2026-07-28 specification revision of the Model Context Protocol removes the initial handshake and protocol-level sessions, introducing a stateless architecture where requests carry context and versioning directly in metadata. Server authors must update handlers to support the stateless option, remove session dependencies, enforce required request headers, and replace mid-call interactive workflows with a multi-round-trip input request pattern.

articles.title: MIT and Sakana AI make self-improving agents cheaper to evaluate
articles.summary: SIFT uses an LLM judge to rank proposed coding-agent improvements before spending compute on full benchmark runs. One experiment reached 35.1% accuracy while using substantially less compute than previous search approaches.

articles.title: Wake me up when AI can…
articles.summary: Compilation of approximately 800 Hacker News comments that defined specific performance benchmarks for artificial intelligence and public votes to determine which AI milestones users believe have been reached.

articles.title: Amazon builds a tiny open model for agent decisions
articles.summary: Amazon's open-source Strands Decider 2B is designed to make fast routing and decision calls inside agent workflows without requiring a large frontier model.

articles.title: New Citrix NetScalar Issue Emerges
articles.summary: Citrix NetScaler administrators are facing recurring appliance reboots caused by an authentication daemon crash when processing crafted SAML authentication traffic following recent security patches.
